listing.name: Newsworthy: Calm News
listing.subtitle: World news, rated
listing.promotionalText: World news, rated by significance. A score and one sentence, a week of developments, and Home Screen widgets in light or dark.
listing.description:
World news, rated by significance.

Newsworthy assesses the significance of world news. Each reading has a score from 1 to 10, a brief explanation and an update time. Higher scores mean more consequential developments. The displayed score fades as developments age.

THE PAST WEEK, IN ONE LIST
Below the reading, the past week's developments: one entry for each, in the order Newsworthy first covered it, with its story and how long ago it broke. The list ends at one week, and Settings can hide it.

STORY AND AGE
Under the sentence, a quieter line first says when Newsworthy last checked the news, then names the story and how long ago it was first reported, such as "US Iran War · 5h ago". Tap the line to switch between the two. For two hours after Newsworthy begins covering a development, its sentence starts with a bold "New:".

HOME SCREEN WIDGETS
Small and medium widgets show the reading and when it was last checked. Each widget has its own settings: show or hide the app name, and choose Follow device, Light or Dark. Widget refresh timing is controlled by your device.

NOTIFICATIONS AT YOUR CHOSEN SCORE
Choose the minimum score you want to hear about in Settings. Notifications are off by default; when enabled, the initial minimum is 8. Receive a notification when the displayed reading meets your choice, without repeated alerts for routine updates to the same development. Tap a notification to open the current reading. Notifications depend on connectivity and your device settings and are not an emergency service.

YOUR APPEARANCE AND SAVED READING
Choose Follow device, Light or Dark in Settings. After an online launch, the last downloaded reading stays available offline with its original timestamp. Share the reading using your device's share sheet. Privacy and Support are in Settings.

ONE-TIME PURCHASE
The download purchase helps offset the cost of running the service. No subscription, in-app purchases or ads. No account or login is required.

Ratings can be wrong. Newsworthy provides general news context, not a complete briefing, an emergency alert or a measure of personal safety. Readings update periodically and saved readings may be outdated. Check the displayed update time.

review.notes:
Version 1.0.1

Settings adds Send Feedback, which opens a pre-filled email in the user's own mail app, and a Publisher page. No new data collection.

Below the sentence a muted line shows "Checked 5m ago", then the story and its age ("US Iran War · 5h ago"); tap to switch. A bold "New:" starts the sentence only in a development's first two hours, so it is often absent.

The past week's timeline is on by default: scroll down or tap the chevron.

1. Physical-device demonstration

Our September 24 review reply includes newsworthy-review-2026-09-24-demo.mp4, recorded on a physical iPhone with build 21. It shows launch, reading, small/medium widgets, notification thresholds and appearance. This historical recording does not show the timeline or per-widget settings.

2. Purpose and audience

Newsworthy assesses world news with a score from 1 to 10, a brief explanation and an update time. It serves people seeking a concise indication of news significance and a bounded view of recent developments. Higher scores mean greater consequence; scores fade as developments age. Ratings can be wrong. It is not an emergency service or a complete briefing.

3. Setup and features

Launch online and continue through the introduction. The public reading loads automatically. No account, login, credentials or sample files are needed.

Scroll down or use the chevron below the reading to see the timeline. Tap the wordmark or iOS status bar to return to the reading. The gear opens Settings, where Show timeline can hide it.

In Settings, open Notifications, enable High-score alerts and allow the iOS permission. Threshold offers a minimum from 5 to 10 (initially 8). Enabling it does not immediately generate a notification. Delivery depends on qualifying readings, connectivity and device settings; routine updates do not repeatedly notify the same development. Foreground notifications refresh the reading without a banner or sound. Tap a notification to open the reading. Turn High-score alerts off to stop delivery.

Add a small or medium widget through the Home Screen picker. Long-press it and choose Edit Widget to show/hide the app name or choose Follow device, Light or Dark independently for each widget. iOS controls refresh timing. Tap it to open the app. The app's Appearance preference is separate. Share opens the system share sheet. The last downloaded reading remains available offline with its original timestamp. Privacy and Support are in Settings.

This is a one-time paid download with no additional paid features, in-app purchases, subscriptions or ads. No user accounts or user-generated content exist; account deletion and content reporting/blocking do not apply.

4. External services

The app and widgets read Newsworthy's HTTPS API on Vercel. Neon PostgreSQL stores readings and optional notification registrations/delivery records. Expo relays notifications through Apple Push Notification service. Tokens and thresholds support delivery, not advertising or tracking.

The backend uses Anthropic Claude and web search to assess public news and group developments. Authorized external AI operators can submit through a private API; it is not public posting. No app-user profile, location or authored text goes to news models. Hosting processes technical information described in the privacy policy. Expo/React Native/EAS build the app; WidgetKit provides widgets. Apple handles the purchase. Support uses email; sharing uses the OS share sheet.

5. Regions

The same English-language content and features are offered across configured regions. Times follow the device locale/time zone. Pricing, taxes and availability vary by storefront; connectivity and OS scheduling affect delivery.

6. Regulated services and third-party material

Newsworthy provides general news context, not regulated professional services. It shows generated scores, short factual sentences and original artwork, not publisher articles or media feeds.
